subject: SLA incident: Sept 9 throttling — postmortem & QBR package
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Sanders <ops_lead@acmehealth.com>, support@acmehealth.com
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SLA incident: Sept 9 throttling — postmortem & QBR package

Team / Tom,

Summary (short): on 2026-09-09 from ~02:14–02:46 UTC we observed sustained request throttling for the public text-generation endpoint in the us-west-2 cluster that resulted in an SLO miss for the 99th percentile latency for 32 minutes. Impact: ~4% of customer requests saw >2s tail latency; Acme Health saw increased API errors on their ingest pipeline and reported downstream job retries. No data exfiltration.

Root cause (short): a throttling regression triggered by a change to the batching heuristic + an unexpected workload spike from a large customer rollout. The runtime backpressure loop took longer to stabilize due to an edge-case in KV cache eviction logic (root cause: memory pressure + batching threshold regression).

Key metrics:
- Incident window: 2026-09-09T02:14:00Z — 2026-09-09T02:46:00Z
- Duration: 32 minutes
- Customers affected (est): 14 accounts, 2 enterprise customers (including Acme Health)
- SLOs breached: p99 latency for text-generation (1h window)
- Observed increase in 5xx rate: peak +0.9% absolute

Actions taken (immediate):
1) Scoped and rolled back batching heuristic change at 02:28 UTC — owner: infra-release (actioned by Marcus Lin) — done.
2) Emergency config change to reduce max concurrent batch window at 02:33 UTC — owner: Karthik Iyer — done.
3) Customer communication: initial ack to affected customers at 03:05 UTC — owner: CS (tom / ops) — done.

Postmortem draft & asks for leadership/QBR pack:
- Attached: postmortem-draft.pdf (internal), incident-timeline.csv. I prepared a customer-facing note draft (customer-note-draft.md) under attachments; Laura please review customer wording.
- Decision needed: recommend SLA credit calculation approach for impacted Acme (proposal: pro-rata credits for the 32-minute window using monthly committed usage). Vivek / Finance sign-off required.
- OKR alignment: propose we add a short-term ORK to stabilize batching heuristics—owner infra & SRE, target: <30m tail regressions for GA workloads; deliverable for QBR.
- Leadership asks for QBR slides: one-page incident summary, action register (owners + due dates), customer impact + credit recommendation. Deliverable: deck-ready slide by 2026-09-14 EOD PT.

Open action register (short):
A1) Finalize postmortem text and customer note — owner: Laura Bennett — due 2026-09-12 17:00 PT
A2) SLA credit calc + approval — owner: Vivek Kulkarni — due 2026-09-13 12:00 PT
A3) Kernel-level fix for KV eviction edge-case — owner: Marcus Lin — due 2026-10-01
A4) Short-term mitigation: conservative batching thresholds & monitoring alert — owner: Karthik Iyer — due 2026-09-15
A5) QBR-ready slide + OKR wording — owner: Mina Haddad — due 2026-09-14 17:00 PT

Tom — can you confirm the customer-observed impact details we captured in the attached timeline? If you prefer a separate joint customer note with Acme branding, we can produce one once Laura signs off.

Thanks — please review and add any items I missed.

--
Mina Haddad
VP, Product Operations
Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.com

Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA incident: Sept 9 throttling — postmortem & QBR package

Thanks for the crisp write-up Mina — exactly the level we need for QBR. Two quick items:

1) SLA credit approach: I prefer the pro-rata method but want legal/finance to sign off. Laura, can you and I sync with Finance? If we need a one-off concession (full month credit, etc.) we'll escalate.
2) OKR framing: keep it tight — "Reduce tail-regression incidents attributable to batching heuristics to 0 in Q4 (metric: incidents/month)". I'll add a leadership ask re: SRE headcount if the mitigation needs a sustained on-call overhead.

Also, can we get an explicit customer impact line for the slide: "Acme Health: delayed nightly ingest jobs for 3x retries (approx. 2 hours of delayed processing)" — Tom pls confirm.

Vivek
Chief Product Officer

Thanks for the quick work and clarity. A couple notes from Acme's side:
- Confirmed: our nightly ingest jobs retried 3x and some backfills ran into the next day; we estimate ~1.8 hours of additional processing cost on our infra.
- For the customer-facing note, we prefer a shared statement approach — if Redwood can provide a joint timeline and remediation commitments, that would be ideal.
- Regarding credits: we'll accept a pro-rata credit if the calculation is transparent and we get the credit applied within the next billing cycle.

One ask: can you confirm the monitoring/alert changes that will prevent a repeat? We want to include that in our internal RCA.
